name: Iron fortification impact on perinatal maternal mortality BOTEC
summary: Adds iron to staple foods to prevent anemia; this sheet looks at deaths around pregnancy and childbirth. GiveWell's spreadsheet "Iron fortification impact on perinatal maternal mortality BOTEC", linked from its grant page. Every number is traced from the sheet's bottom line; calculated rows reproduce the sheet's own values.

rows.explainer: Total population (all ages, both sexes) deaths for “maternal disorders” in Sub-Saharan Africa according to the Global Burden of Disease Results Tool = 8.75 per 100,000. This is broader than what we're specifically examining but can serve as an upper bound. GBD Results Tool

rows.label: Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for programs that mostly buy and hand out goods (nets, drugs, supplements, vaccines, water treatment): staff pay is a small part of the cost. Our judgment; we haven't seen this program's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Delivery staff are mostly hired locally at local rates, so the gap is small. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
